evidence.title: AI in Zed
evidence.finding: Native, ACP and terminal agents, parallel threads, model access paths and context tools.

evidence.title: Collaboration
evidence.finding: Simultaneous editing with cursors, channels and voice; project filesystem shared.

evidence.title: Remote development
evidence.finding: Local UI and model communication; SSH server runs source/tools, automatic server install.

evidence.locator: Currently Working On; Coming Up Next

evidence.title: AI overview
evidence.finding: Zed separates its native agent, external ACP agents and terminal threads, with several threads running across projects.

evidence.title: LLM providers
evidence.finding: Native Zed AI has hosted, API, subscription, gateway and local model setup routes; these settings do not configure external agents.

evidence.title: Agent panel
evidence.finding: Independent threads have history and optional worktrees. Steer works for Zed Agent, while external-agent history and token support vary.

evidence.title: Remote development
evidence.finding: Local UI and model communication remain local while source files, language servers, tasks and terminals run on an SSH server.

evidence.title: Collaboration
evidence.finding: Signed-in users can simultaneously edit a shared project and use channels and voice; project sharing exposes its local filesystem.

evidence.title: Sandboxing
evidence.finding: OS sandboxing covers Zed Agent terminal/fetch tools, not external agents or terminal threads; platform-specific limits apply.

evidence.title: Tool permissions
evidence.finding: Tool rules support allow, deny and confirm; deny takes precedence and built-in security rules cannot be overridden.

evidence.title: AI privacy
evidence.locator: AI request paths; retention and training
evidence.finding: Zed describes no default retention of prompts/code and separates hosted commitments from own-provider terms; some models have safety-retention exceptions.

evidence.title: Telemetry in Zed
evidence.finding: Client metrics and diagnostics can be disabled; hosted AI/collaboration metadata remains necessary for those services.

evidence.title: Plans & pricing
evidence.finding: The editor works without an account. Pro includes $5 monthly usage, metered at provider list price plus 10%, with configurable spend limits.

evidence.title: Git
evidence.finding: Zed displays working tree, staging and branch state with native Git controls; unsupported operations can use the terminal.

evidence.title: Zed pinned README
evidence.finding: This pinned README states primarily GPL-3.0-or-later with Apache-2.0 components where marked; hosted-service parity does not follow.

evidence.title: Zed roadmap
evidence.locator: Currently working on; Coming up next
evidence.finding: The roadmap lists async collaboration in progress and Web and Plan Mode next; undated plans are not current capabilities.

evidence.title: CLI Reference
evidence.finding: Product-owned zed CLI opens files/directories, remote projects and diff views; wait/reuse/add options integrate with other tools. This is an editor launcher, not a headless agent API.

evidence.title: External Agents
evidence.locator: Registry; Common agents; Configuration; Custom agents
evidence.finding: Zed ACP registry supports Claude, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor and Pi among others. Custom ACP command/args/env adapters are configurable. External auth/tools/retention remain agent owned.

evidence.title: Parallel Agents
evidence.finding: Threads run independently with different native/external agents, own history and context. History archives/restores/deletes, agent-dependent imports and detached-HEAD worktree save/restore are documented.

evidence.title: Agent Panel
evidence.finding: Panel supports queued/steer messages, native thread history and summaries, per-hunk keep/reject, multi-buffer review, context attachments and token counts. External integration feature parity varies.

evidence.title: Tools
evidence.finding: Native tools include grep/find/read, diagnostics, fetch/search_web, file edits, terminal and spawn_agent with a separate context window. Pro/Zed-provider-only web search is distinct from MCP search.

evidence.title: Agent Settings
evidence.finding: Subagents inherit model/effort/speed by default or use agent.subagent_model. Requested models preserve configured controls with documented fallback; compaction defaults to ninety percent context.

evidence.title: MCP
evidence.finding: Zed connects local/remote MCP servers through configuration/extensions with headers or OAuth. Native profiles and per-tool permission rules apply; ACP forwarding and external native config are separate.

evidence.title: Instructions
evidence.finding: Personal AGENTS.md and compatible project instruction files provide persistent context; project rules override personal instructions. External/terminal agents have their own loaders.

evidence.title: Skills
evidence.finding: SKILL.md packages are created/imported, scoped global/project, editable/deletable and shared as self-contained links requiring explicit recipient save. Model-loaded skills follow tool permissions; manual invocation is explicit.

evidence.title: Agent Profiles
evidence.finding: Write enables edits/commands, Ask is read-only and Minimal has no project tools. Profiles set tool availability and default model; permission rules are separate and external agents do not inherit these profiles.

evidence.title: Tool Permissions
evidence.finding: Native tools support allow/deny/confirm patterns. Hardcoded protections and always_deny outrank auto-approve; chained shell commands are individually checked. ACP/terminal-agent boundaries remain separate.

evidence.title: Dev Containers
evidence.finding: Zed builds/opens devcontainers with Docker or Podman and runs tasks, terminals and language servers there. Config changes do not rebuild automatically; users restart and reopen.

evidence.title: Roles
evidence.finding: Business organizations use Owner, Admin, Billing Manager and Member with explicit administration/feature/billing rights. Removing membership revokes org-managed access without disabling personal editor use.

evidence.title: Channels
evidence.finding: Channels offer real-time shared code editing, voice and Markdown notes. Guests are read-only unless temporarily granted write access. Unsharing disconnects collaborators; terminal following is not supported.

evidence.title: Use a Local Model
evidence.finding: Native Zed features work with local llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio or an OpenAI-compatible server using configured model/base URL. Endpoint auth is customer controlled.

evidence.title: Authenticate with Zed
evidence.finding: Editor use needs no login. Own-key AI can work without Zed sign-in; hosted models and real-time collaboration require Zed’s GitHub OAuth account.

evidence.title: AI Privacy
evidence.finding: Zed normally retains no prompt/code context; provider contracts prohibit training but designated safety-retention models are exceptions to ZDR. Feedback/training sharing is explicit opt-in. BYOK/external/terminal paths follow their own providers.

evidence.title: Telemetry in Zed
evidence.finding: Client metrics/crashes can be disabled independently. Hosted-service metadata needed for billing/rate limiting remains required; account-linked random IDs and inspectable logs are documented.

evidence.title: Plans & Pricing
evidence.finding: Free editor includes own-key and external-agent use. Pro is ten dollars monthly with five token dollars; hosted usage is provider list plus ten percent. Trial is fourteen days/no card and shares balance with Delta; no Delta execution capability is inferred.

evidence.title: Developing Zed
evidence.finding: Vendor developer documentation identifies Rust crates, GPU-accelerated GPUI, native editor/project/workspace components and a separate collaboration server.

evidence.title: Use an Existing Subscription
evidence.finding: ChatGPT Plus/Pro authenticates as a native Zed provider without API key; Claude Pro/Max uses external Claude or CLI. OpenCode uses API keys; Cursor uses its external/CLI route.

evidence.title: Zed Agent sandboxing
evidence.finding: Native sandbox blocks terminal networking and out-of-scope writes by default when enabled. macOS uses Seatbelt, Linux Bubblewrap and Windows WSL Bubblewrap only. Non-terminal fetch does not inherit terminal network limits.

evidence.title: Zed stable releases
evidence.finding: Stable-release notes publish current shipped editor fixes and new features. This source pass did not install or benchmark the release.

evidence.title: Zed Git documentation (v1.27.0)
evidence.locator: docs/src/git.md lines 168-258 (Committing, Branch Management, Git Worktrees, Merge Conflicts), release v1.27.0 commit c84af5b
evidence.finding: The Git Panel commits staged changes and can undo the last commit, creates, switches and deletes branches, creates and switches linked worktrees from a picker, and shows merge conflicts with per-conflict resolution buttons.

evidence.title: Zed Git Panel create_pull_request
evidence.locator: crates/git_ui/src/git_panel.rs lines 5064-5115 (GitPanel::create_pull_request), registered as the git CreatePullRequest action in crates/git_ui/src/git_ui.rs line 188, release v1.27.0 commit c84af5b
evidence.finding: The Create Pull Request action builds the hosting provider's create-pull-request URL for the tracked upstream branch and opens it in the browser; Zed itself does not create or manage the pull request.

local_creation.answer: Users create native or installed external-agent threads from the panel/sidebar.

supported_edits.answer: Sent messages can be edited and resubmitted with revised prompts/context.

instructions.answer: Zed Agent loads personal AGENTS.md and the first matching compatible project instruction file.

skills.answer: Native SKILL.md packages load on demand or through /slash and @ mentions.

project_docs.answer: Project guidance can use .rules, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md and other documented compatibility paths.

scope.answer: Skills are global under ~/.agents/skills or project-local .agents/skills.

provenance.answer: Imported/shared skills show their body and target path; a recipient must explicitly save a shared skill.

correction.answer: Users edit the personal/project instruction files to change persistent guidance.

deletion.answer: Skills Manager deletes the installed folder.

code_search.answer: Native find_path and regex grep navigate project files.

external_knowledge.answer: Files, directories, symbols, previous threads, diagnostics, diffs and fetched URLs can be attached as context.

multimodal_inputs.answer: Vision-capable providers accept images via mention, drag/drop or paste.

access_scope.answer: search_web is Pro-only with the Zed provider; other configurations can use a search MCP server.

citations.answer: Pasted code selections retain their file-context mention.

persistent_requirements.answer: Persistent channel Markdown notes can hold design/status ideas, but are not a typed requirements object.

human_edits.answer: Channel members collaboratively edit Markdown notes.

later_retrieval.answer: Channel notes can be opened without joining its call.

concurrent_tasks.answer: Multiple threads can receive independent tasks while previous threads continue.

quotas.answer: Docs permit multiple concurrent threads but give no numerical product concurrency quota.

roles.answer: Native spawn_agent delegates a bounded task to a subagent with a separate context window.

model_harness_effort.answer: agent.subagent_model configures subagent model, thinking, effort and speed; otherwise the native child inherits its parent’s settings.

results_return.answer: Subagent work returns an outcome to the parent when only its result is needed.

orchestration_owner.answer: The built-in Zed Agent invokes spawn_agent rather than requiring an external coordinator.

activation.answer: The parent uses its built-in spawn_agent tool during a task.

followup.answer: Resuming a subagent preserves its existing model, reasoning and speed settings.

pause.answer: A stop button interrupts execution; a distinct durable pause mechanism is not established.

notifications.answer: Waiting/completion notifications can be enabled visually and audibly.

pending_decisions.answer: Permission-gated tool actions request human confirmation before running.

retained_history.answer: Native threads retain conversation history and can start fresh from a summary.

presets.answer: Native Write, Ask and Minimal profiles provide different tool sets.

agent_configuration.answer: Native thread settings and subagent model/effort/speed can be configured separately.

in_run_changes.answer: Later parent model/effort changes do not update already configured/requested child models.

discoverability.answer: The panel’s profile selector exposes Configure and custom-profile creation.

local.answer: Native agent terminal tools run shell commands in the project environment.

self_hosted.answer: Zed Remote Development uses a local UI and customer-hosted headless server connected over SSH.

provisioning.answer: The local client builds/launches the configured devcontainer using installed Docker/Podman.

payer.answer: The user supplies and pays for the remote server or devcontainer host.

resources.answer: The user supplies local UI hardware and remote host compute.

checkout.answer: A new agent worktree has its own checkout.

branch.answer: New worktrees start detached HEAD; a branch is selected/created separately.

container.answer: Zed opens projects inside devcontainers using Docker or Podman; tasks/terminals run in that container.

filesystem.answer: Workspace files are linked into the container according to the devcontainer specification.

code_separation.answer: Separate worktrees prevent overlapping working files; model conversations remain independent.

task_resume.answer: Archived native threads can be restored, including their removed linked worktree.

state_reconstruction.answer: Archiving an unused linked worktree saves its Git state; restoration recreates it.

manual_repair.answer: External thread import/history support varies; Cursor/Gemini CLI imports are explicitly not supported.

dependencies.answer: Project devcontainer.json defines the container image, dependencies and environment.

services.answer: Language servers, tasks and terminals run on the user’s remote server.

ports.answer: SSH port forwarding is configurable per remote project.

remote_setup.answer: Open in Container builds the image if needed, launches the container and reconnects the project.

automatic_repair.answer: Changes to devcontainer.json do not automatically rebuild/reload the container; users must stop it and reopen.

token_limits.answer: Automatic compaction defaults at ninety percent of context; a configurable threshold or /compact is supported.

spend_limits.answer: Pro/Business set pre-tax monthly hosted-token spend limits; included credit is separate.

enforcement.answer: Hosted-model use stops when the configured limit is reached until reset or administrator increase.

logs.answer: The thread transcript shows streamed responses and tools in use.

task_stats.answer: Panel surfaces active-thread token usage and edited-file/line counts.

tokens.answer: Active native threads show token usage near the model/profile selector.

drilldown.answer: The current thread exposes token counts; complete cross-harness invoice reconciliation is not established.

visibility.answer: Collaborators see shared files, cursors, navigation and edits, and guests can view read-only.

comments.answer: Channels have a shared Markdown notes document for design/status discussion.

plan_restrictions.answer: Business organization collaboration can be disabled by admin policy.

owner_online.answer: Shared project code is hosted on the sharer’s machine; unsharing disconnects participants.

organization_roles.answer: Business organizations have Owner, Admin, Billing Manager and Member.

membership.answer: Owners/Admins invite by email, change roles and remove non-owner members.

unauthorized_access.answer: Members cannot access billing/admin settings; Billing Managers have billing but no paid Business AI seat.

revocation.answer: Removal ends organization-managed settings and feature access while personal Zed remains usable.

plan_scope.answer: These role rights apply to Zed Business organizations.

command.answer: Native terminal commands are matched against regex allow/deny/confirm rules, including chained subcommands.

tool.answer: Profiles determine tool availability; permission rules separately govern confirmations.

lifetime.answer: Rules persist in the user/project settings file until changed.

allow.answer: always_allow or a global allow default auto-approves eligible actions.

deny.answer: always_deny blocks matching actions even when global permission default allows.

safer_modes.answer: Ask removes edit/terminal tools for read-only questions; Minimal uses no project tools.

enforcement.answer: Hardcoded security rules and always_deny outrank allow; always_confirm can force approval.

cross_session_persistence.answer: Thread History retains archived conversations across projects until deleted.

retention.answer: Permanent deletion removes conversation history and associated worktree data, and cannot be undone.

change_understanding.answer: Review Changes opens a multi-buffer view of all agent-edited files and changed-line counts.

evidence_navigation.answer: Edited-file accordion and Review Changes navigate the affected files.

request_changes.answer: Users keep or reject individual hunks or the whole agent change set.

keyboard.answer: Review Changes has a documented keyboard shortcut.

retained_context.answer: File/line review remains alongside the agent conversation.

tests.answer: The native terminal tool can run repository tests and return command output.

types.answer: The diagnostics tool reads file or project errors/warnings after edits.

required_checks.answer: Tool access permits tests/diagnostics; no universal mandatory delivery check is established.

grouping.answer: Multi-buffer review groups the thread’s changed files.

artifacts.answer: The review surface shows actual file diffs.

next_actions.answer: Review controls keep or reject hunks or all changes.

source_visibility.answer: Zed’s public repository and build guides cover macOS, Linux and Windows. Main source is GPL-3.0-or-later with Apache-2.0 components where marked.

self_hosting.answer: The native editor/agent can use locally hosted llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio or customer-compatible endpoints on user infrastructure.

vendor_dependencies.answer: Local/native core use can avoid Zed-hosted models; real-time collaboration and Zed-hosted inference remain vendor services.

import.answer: Thread History imports supported external-agent threads; Cursor and Gemini CLI are currently excluded.

account_independence.answer: Editor and own-key AI work without Zed sign-in; hosted models and real-time collaboration require authentication.

history_portability.answer: Archived native threads restore within Zed; a general cross-product transcript export format remains unestablished.

code_data.answer: Zed does not retain prompt or code context by default; opt-in feedback/data sharing is separate.

prompts.answer: Hosted model requests route through Zed to its providers under no-training contracts.

credentials.answer: Provider keys saved through Zed are stored in the system keychain, not settings.json.

logs.answer: Users inspect client telemetry through zed: open telemetry log.

retention.answer: Most hosted inference has ZDR; provider-designated safety-retention models retain prompts/outputs under provider rules, including at least thirty days for named Anthropic Covered Models.

training.answer: Zed-hosted providers commit not to train on prompts/code; optional feedback or edit-prediction training requires explicit sharing.

subprocessors.answer: Telemetry documentation names Sentry, Snowflake, Hex and Amplitude for diagnostics/analytics.

telemetry_controls.answer: telemetry.diagnostics=false and telemetry.metrics=false disable client reports; hosted-service rate-limit/billing metadata is required.

consent_prompt.answer: Conversation feedback and eligible edit-prediction data are retained only through explicit sharing/opt-in.

provider_separation.answer: BYOK, subscription, gateway, local-model, external-agent and terminal paths use their own provider handling.

currency.answer: Plans and token allowances are quoted in US dollars.

included_usage.answer: Pro includes five dollars of hosted-model token credit monthly.

trial.answer: Fourteen-day Pro trial includes five dollars of designated-model usage and predictions; no card required.

model_cost.answer: Hosted inference is provider list pricing plus ten percent.

free_scenarios.answer: Free editor supports user API keys and external agents; paid hosted-model costs remain separate.

usage_caps.answer: Pro monthly token allowance is five dollars; the student plan is capped at ten dollars monthly.

paid_evaluation.answer: Trial automatically reverts to Free after fourteen days; it does not auto-enroll in paid Pro.

units.answer: Hosted-model usage is metered in tokens and converted to dollars.

included_limits.answer: Included hosted-model credit resets on the monthly billing date.

overages.answer: Usage above the allowance is billed at hosted-model rates, bounded by configured spend limits.

transparency_classification.answer: Public base price, included token allowance, model markup and spend-limit mechanics are documented; fixed workload costs remain unknown.
